what_it_is.prose: Thales S.A. (Euronext Paris: HO) is a French listed defence-electronics OEM headquartered in Courbevoie. In the Indian military-aerospace context, Thales's most significant footprint is on the Dassault Rafale: Thales supplies the RBE2 active-electronically-scanned-array (AESA) radar, the SPECTRA internal electronic-warfare and self-protection suite, Front Sector Optronics (FSO), the TALIOS targeting pod and cockpit displays — collectively about 25% of the aircraft's value. Under a 2017 transfer-of-technology arrangement tied to the Rafale offset, Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) manufactures the transmit/receive (T/R) modules for the RBE2 radar front end in India; the first BEL-built front end was delivered in November 2020 and the 7,000th T/R module in February 2025, with BEL also beginning production of microwave modules for the SPECTRA EW suite. Thales's India presence is further anchored by two joint ventures: BEL-Thales Systems Limited (BTSL, incorporated 28 August 2014, BEL 74% / Thales 26%, Bengaluru) co-developing radars including the Multi-Target Tracking Radar and PHAROS fire-control radar; and the Thales-Reliance Defence joint venture announced on 21 June 2017 (Thales 49% / Reliance 51%) at the Mihan-Nagpur SEZ for radar and EW sensors, microwave technologies and high-performance airborne electronics. Thales also contributes avionics to the Airbus C-295 India programme.

deployments_procurement.summary: Thales's India military-aerospace footprint centres on the Rafale (36 IAF aircraft; 26 Rafale Marine ordered 2025), for which it supplies the RBE2 AESA radar, SPECTRA EW suite and optronics, with BEL now building the radar T/R modules in India under ToT. Two joint ventures — BEL-Thales Systems Limited (2014, Bengaluru) and Thales-Reliance Defence (2017, Nagpur) — localise radar, EW and airborne-electronics work. Thales also contributes avionics to the Airbus C-295 programme.

faq.question: What is Thales's role on the Rafale in Indian service?
faq.answer: Thales supplies roughly a quarter of the Rafale's value in mission electronics: the RBE2 active-electronically-scanned-array (AESA) radar, the SPECTRA internal electronic-warfare and self-protection suite, Front Sector Optronics (FSO), the TALIOS targeting pod and cockpit displays. Under a transfer-of-technology arrangement, Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) manufactures the RBE2 radar's transmit/receive modules in India — the 7,000th module was delivered in February 2025.

faq.question: What Thales joint ventures operate in India?
faq.answer: Two principal ones. BEL-Thales Systems Limited (BTSL) was incorporated on 28 August 2014 (BEL 74% / Thales 26%, Bengaluru) to co-develop radars including the Multi-Target Tracking Radar and the PHAROS fire-control radar. Separately, a Thales-Reliance Defence joint venture (Thales 49% / Reliance 51%) was announced on 21 June 2017 at the Mihan-Nagpur SEZ for radar and electronic-warfare sensors, microwave technologies and high-performance airborne electronics.

faq.question: Is the Rafale's SPECTRA electronic-warfare suite being made in India?
faq.answer: The SPECTRA self-protection suite is a Thales design. As of 2025, BEL had begun manufacturing microwave modules for SPECTRA in India, extending the Make-in-India localisation that started with the RBE2 radar's T/R modules. The core SPECTRA electronic-warfare intellectual property remains with Thales.
